memory_candidates.content: When bulk-editing an identical, copy-templated section across many agent contract files, first verify byte-for-byte identity across the set (grep -c on a distinguishing string, then a full Read diff of at least one pair) before scripting the substitution. Use an exact-match Python string.replace with a pre-flight occurrence-count check (== 1) per file rather than sed/regex, so any file that has silently drifted from the template fails loudly instead of being mis-edited.

When removing a section that carries the only instance of an otherwise-needed instruction (e.g. a dispatch_seq echo scoped to 'the handoff's own field'), redirect the instruction's target rather than deleting it outright. Silently dropping instructions when replacing a boilerplate section can regress unrelated behavior that depended on that boilerplate as its sole carrier.

For a template-copied instruction spread across N extension agent files, prove consistency with a repo-wide grep for both the removed old phrasing (expect zero hits) and the new canonical phrasing (expect N hits), rather than a three-file spot check. This is the reusable acceptance test that also catches future authors reintroducing the old template.
